data.narrative:
PLD Space is a SPAC-stage space & aerospace company founded by Raúl Torres, Raúl Verdú, and José Enrique Martínez, having raised €120M to date. The valuation universe comprises 5 public comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including Impulse Space, Starcloud, SpaceX, and Sierra Space.

Standard triangulation methods encounter significant constraints. Peer-median multiples cannot be applied: the Space & Aerospace sector contains 11 total comparable companies, but filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier peers yields fewer than 3 datapoints—the minimum threshold for statistical reliability. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples is similarly inapplicable; while the sector median P/S stands at 23.9x across the 6 public tickers listed, PLD Space's revenue is not disclosed, precluding the calculation of an implied valuation.

Given these data constraints, a quantitative valuation range cannot be reliably synthesized. The analysis exposes a fundamental gap: private frontier-tech companies at the SPAC stage rarely report revenue, and the peer set lacks sufficient depth within narrow filters to support defensible multiples. Resolution would require either disclosure of PLD Space's forward or trailing revenue, or identification of additional same-stage private comparables with known transaction multiples. Without these inputs, any range would rest on assumption rather than triangulation.
